title: Predicting Stock Returns and Maximizing Return on Investment Using Clustering Analysis of Financial Statements
content: Stock investing can be pursued through speculation, which seeks short-term gains from price movements, or through long-term investment, commonly guided by a buy-and-hold strategy oriented toward return on investment (ROI) and dividend distribution. While machine learning has been applied extensively to the speculation side of this problem, comparatively little attention has been paid to the investment side, particularly to frameworks that incorporate company financial statements to guide long-term buy, hold, or sell decisions. This paper proposes a clustering-based framework that addresses this gap. Quarterly financial-statement data for Tesla, obtained from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, is reduced from 58 raw features to a 23-feature subset using Binary Particle Swarm Optimization, then partitioned with K-means clustering into groups representing financial stability, growth, and decline. Two clustering configurations are compared: financial-statement features alone, and financial-statement features merged with speculation-side data (historical prices, social media sentiment, and news sentiment) drawn from a previously published ensemble-regression price-prediction system. The merged configuration is found to produce a more coherent three-cluster partition, with a silhouette score of 0.692 and a Davies–Bouldin index of 0.277, compared with 0.515 and 0.636 for the financial-statement-only configuration. Each resulting cluster is interpreted as a Buy, Keep, or Sell recommendation and applied to sixteen quarters of Tesla data spanning 2019 to 2022, producing recommendations that align with major company events such as the 2022 valuation decline. The results indicate that combining financial-statement analysis with speculation-side data through clustering is a practical route to ROI-oriented investment guidance that complements existing price-prediction approaches.
